changelog: v147: new Answers view (System menu, next to Source Integrity) lists every answer newest-first with question, category, date, and word count, each linking to reflect/correct/retract — filing here is synchronous, so there's no in-flight status column like the hosted twin's. Also, the local compiled-wiki viewer now works on a phone: at 820px and below, the full wiki navigation opens as a drawer instead of disappearing; search and the Views menu remain available, controls have phone-sized tap targets, and regular pages stay within the viewport while wide tables keep their own intentional scroll. Also, Source Integrity now opens each manifested raw answer or source as a rendered, read-only body in the owner-only local viewer, with direct links between the body, its integrity record, and reflection/correction/retraction actions. The raw-body route requires a loopback peer and Host, never caches or writes on GET, and reads exact regular files through one manifest-gated, no-follow descriptor walk that rejects traversal, encoding tricks, absolute paths, NULs, directories, untracked files, and all symlinks. Also, direct on-machine OpenAI-compatible models are now a first-class provider for the whole Lifehug Loop. Configure an Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, or equivalent endpoint/model/timeout once and compile, classification, research, entity rosters, the Mirror, artifact revision, and connector dossiers all use it. Local routing is loopback-only and fail-closed by default: its transport bypasses proxy environment variables and rejects redirects, while an invalid, timed-out, malformed, or offline server returns to the existing agent-task path without silently sending private source material to a cloud fallback. `ai-status` explicitly performs a non-mutating readiness probe and reports provider and model, while viewer discovery remains network-free. Deliberate OpenClaw, Kimi, and Anthropic routes remain available, and the optional Anthropic SDK keeps v122's keyless/no-process-exit behavior. The shared router uses only Python's standard library and never logs prompts, source bodies, responses, or secrets.
